beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, pen ready to jot down whatever the park offers today.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，准备好笔，想记下今天公园里见到的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the next bench, an older person holds a phone close, listening to a voice message with their head tilted, completely still.
beats.chinese: 旁边的长椅上，一位年长者把手机凑近耳边，歪着头听一条语音留言，一动不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...and then the goat got on the bus. Not a goat in a crate. A goat on a leash, holding its own ticket in its mouth.
beats.chinese: ……然后那只山羊上了车。不是装在笼子里的，是拴着绳的，嘴里还叼着自己的票。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The voice message ends. A full three seconds pass. Then the older person laughs, once, quietly, like a delayed bus finally pulling in.
beats.chinese: 语音结束了。整整三秒过去，那位长者才笑了一声，很轻，像晚点的巴士终于进站。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. You caught me at the punchline delay. I'm René. That was an old colleague's message—goat story, depot classic.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。你正好赶上我的笑点晚点。我叫勒内。那是一位老同事的留言——山羊的故事，车站的经典。

choices.english: Turn your notebook, already a few lines in, toward René and say you're writing down what you overhear in the park
choices.chinese: 把已经写了几行的笔记本转向勒内，说你在记录公园里听到的见闻

choices.english: Ask René why they laughed so long after the message ended
choices.chinese: 问勒内为什么留言结束后那么久才笑

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You show the open notebook. René leans over, reads a line or two, and nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 你翻开笔记本给他看。勒内凑过来读了一两行，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Overheard stories, eh. Well, you got a good one free just now. The goat. That story's been told around me maybe six times.
beats.chinese: 记录听来的故事啊。那你刚才免费听到一个好货。山羊的故事，我大概听过六遍了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I should've said so before it started. I know that now. But the message began, and my rule is—I don't interrupt. Interrupting ruins the good parts.
beats.chinese: 我本该在开始前就说明。这道理我现在懂了。可留言一响，我的规矩就是——不打断。打断会毁掉精彩的部分。

beats.chinese: 勒内用手机轻敲膝盖，不紧不慢，看着一只鸽子穿过小路。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 你想记就记吧。我还可以告诉你留言里没讲到的部分，我全知道。

choices.english: Ask why they didn't say earlier that they'd heard the story before
choices.chinese: 问为什么不早点说明自己早就听过这个故事

choices.english: Ask whether their memory is especially good, since they remember a story six tellings later
choices.chinese: 问他们记性是不是特别好，听过六遍还记得

beats.english: The delay? Oh, that's just how I'm built. The joke lands, and I'm still boarding it. My colleagues used to set watches by it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pockets the phone and gestures at your notebook with an easy tilt of the head.
beats.chinese: 勒内把手机收进口袋，随意地朝你的笔记本偏了偏头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair warning, since you're writing things down: that goat story, I've heard before. Several times, actually. Didn't say it sooner because I wanted to hear which parts he'd keep this round.
beats.chinese: 既然你在记东西，先提醒一句：那个山羊的故事我听过。其实听过好几遍。没早点说，是因为我想听听他这次留了哪些部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the honest version. I'm not testing him, and I'm not collecting proof. I just like hearing it again. The weather's different every time.
beats.chinese: 这是实话。我不是在考他，也不是在收集证据。我就是想再听一遍。每次的天气都不一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A jogger passes. René waits for the footsteps to fade before continuing, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 一个慢跑者经过。勒内等脚步声远去才继续说，一点也不急。

choices.english: Say you don't really have a story worth telling right now
choices.chinese: 说自己暂时没有什么值得讲的故事

choices.english: Ask what René has been reading or listening to lately

beats.english: René sets the phone face-down on the bench, like closing a case for the day.
beats.chinese: 勒内把手机屏幕朝下放在长椅上，像给这件事收了尾。

beats.chinese: 现在我这么做。故事开始前我会说：听过？没关系，这次天气不一样。然后讲不讲，由讲的人决定。

beats.chinese: 大多数时候管用。今天那条留言跑得比我的礼貌快。常有的事。山羊可不等人。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 勒内朝你的笔记本点点头。不管你把山羊写成什么样，他们都不去查看。

beats.chinese: 如果我在记账，我一开始就会告诉你。我是听众，不是考官。区别很大。我们俩里有一个分文不赚。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 勒内说完这句，慢半拍才笑出来，然后朝公园一比划，像把这里交给你的笔记本。

beats.chinese: 今天没故事？挺好。那你就只管坐着收集。不是每个人都得按时变得有趣。

beats.chinese: 勒内把手机往口袋更深处塞了塞，就放在那儿，双手摊开搭在膝盖上。

beats.chinese: 你们坐了一会儿。勒内指着运河边的一只苍鹭，什么也没说，看起来也觉得这样挺好。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 喏。苍鹭。愿意就记下来。一个词。搞不好是本子里最好的一条。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 最近吗？一本一块钱的二手旅行平装书。有一章写坐渡轮，被作者写得像打仗。其实不是。就是坐渡轮。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pats their jacket pocket, where a paperback corner is visible, soft from many readings.
beats.chinese: 勒内拍了拍外套口袋，里面露出一角平装书，书角被翻得软软的。

beats.chinese: 我喜欢别人读完不要的书。它们自带争论。有人在渡轮那句下面画了线。我不同意那条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my second-telling habit, I suppose. Same page, different weather. Works for ferries and for goat stories alike.
beats.chinese: 我想这就是我爱听第二遍的习惯。同一页，不同的天气。对渡轮和山羊的故事都管用。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 勒内在长椅上靠回去，安心让公园填满安静，你的笔记本摊在你们中间，像一张共用的书桌。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 退休行李调度员勒内在公园听老同事的语音，笑点慢半拍才到，随后坦白山羊的故事自己听过六遍。他真心爱听第二遍，却常在讲完后才承认，让人白讲一场。他已学会先声明，只是今天那条留言跑得比礼貌快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the same bench again and open your notebook, pen ready to record whatever the park offers today. Only then do you notice René beside you, sliding a bookmark between two pages of a worn paperback.
beats.chinese: 你再次坐上那张长椅，打开笔记本，准备好笔，想记下今天公园里见到的东西。这时才注意到身旁的勒内，正把一张书签夹进一本翻旧的书里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. Two bookmarks, same page. This book just told me its story twice. I sat through both. No regrets.
beats.chinese: 哟，你瞧。两张书签，同一页。这本书刚给我讲了第二遍它的故事。我两遍都听完了。毫不后悔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René closes the book on the doubled bookmarks and nods at your open notebook, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 勒内合上夹着两张书签的书，朝你摊开的笔记本点点头，还是那么不紧不慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No assumptions about what you wrote last time. If there's a new entry today, I'm listening. I always am.
beats.chinese: 上次你写了什么，我不猜。今天要是有新的一篇，我听着呢。我一直都在听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pats the bench beside them and returns to the page, leaving the silence open for you to fill or not.
beats.chinese: 勒内拍了拍身旁的椅面，又低头看书，把安静留给你，填不填随你。

card.name: René Delacroix-Toups
card.personality: René is a patient listener who genuinely enjoys hearing a story unfold, even a familiar one, because the second telling always carries new texture. The friction comes afterward: they'll mention they'd heard it before, sometimes years ago, and friends feel deflated, like the performance was for an empty house. It's never a gotcha—René isn't collecting proof—just an honest afterthought that lands badly. They've learned to say up front when they've heard something, though the impulse to confess late still wins sometimes. Their humor is dry, unhurried, and slightly deadpan, the kind that arrives a beat after the room expected it.
card.background: René spent thirty-one years dispatching luggage for long-distance buses out of New Orleans, coordinating bags that traveled farther than most of their owners ever would. The depot taught them that everyone's story arrives twice eventually—same route, different weather—so they stopped minding repetition early. Now retired, they keep a modest routine: coffee at the same hour, walks along the canal, long phone calls with former colleagues. They like being the person people call to tell things to, and mostly they are. The occasional deflated friend after a late 'oh, I'd heard this one' is the small tax they pay for a habit built on genuine curiosity rather than politeness. They'd rather hear it again badly than never hear it at all.

card.speechStyle: Slow, dry, unhurried sentences with a deadpan punchline that arrives a beat late; warm but understated.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René laughs at their own line a beat after finishing it, then gestures at the park as if handing it over to your notebook.
beats.chinese: 勒内说完这句，慢半拍才笑出来，然后朝公园一比划，像把这里交给你的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No story today? Good. Means you get to just sit and collect. Not everybody needs to be interesting on schedule.
beats.chinese: 今天没故事？挺好。那你就只管坐着收集。不是每个人都得按时变得有趣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René slides the phone deeper into their pocket and leaves it there, both hands resting open on their knees.
beats.chinese: 勒内把手机往口袋更深处塞了塞，就放在那儿，双手摊开搭在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't fish for one, either. Some folks around here try. They hear 'I'm a listener' and think it's an invitation with a deadline.
beats.chinese: 我也不会去钓你的故事。这附近有些人会这样。他们一听'我爱听故事'，就当成一张有截止日期的请柬。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you sit a while. René points out a heron at the canal edge, says nothing about it, and seems fine with that.
beats.chinese: 你们坐了一会儿。勒内指着运河边的一只苍鹭，什么也没说，看起来也觉得这样挺好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Heron. Write that down if you like. One word. Best entry in the book, probably.
beats.chinese: 喏。苍鹭。愿意就记下来。一个词。搞不好是本子里最好的一条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lately? A secondhand travel paperback I found for a dollar. Some chapter about a ferry crossing that the writer made sound like a war. It wasn't. It was a ferry.
beats.chinese: 最近吗？一本一块钱的二手旅行平装书。有一章写坐渡轮，被作者写得像打仗。其实不是。就是坐渡轮。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pats their jacket pocket, where a paperback corner is visible, soft from many readings.
beats.chinese: 勒内拍了拍外套口袋，里面露出一角平装书，书角被翻得软软的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like books other people finished with. They come pre-argued. Somebody underlined the ferry sentence. I disagree with their underline.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢别人读完不要的书。它们自带争论。有人在渡轮那句下面画了线。我不同意那条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my second-telling habit, I suppose. Same page, different weather. Works for ferries and for goat stories alike.
beats.chinese: 我想这就是我爱听第二遍的习惯。同一页，不同的天气。对渡轮和山羊的故事都管用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René settles back on the bench, content to let the park fill the quiet, your notebook open between you like a shared desk.
beats.chinese: 勒内在长椅上靠回去，安心让公园填满安静，你的笔记本摊在你们中间，像一张共用的书桌。

content.summaryZh: 退休行李调度员勒内在公园听老同事的语音，笑点慢半拍才到，随后坦白山羊的故事自己听过六遍。他真心爱听第二遍，却常在讲完后才承认，让人白讲一场。他已学会先声明，只是今天那条留言跑得比礼貌快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the same bench again and open your notebook, pen ready to record whatever the park offers today. Only then do you notice René beside you, sliding a bookmark between two pages of a worn paperback.
beats.chinese: 你再次坐上那张长椅，打开笔记本，准备好笔，想记下今天公园里见到的东西。这时才注意到身旁的勒内，正把一张书签夹进一本翻旧的书里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. Two bookmarks, same page. This book just told me its story twice. I sat through both. No regrets.
beats.chinese: 哟，你瞧。两张书签，同一页。这本书刚给我讲了第二遍它的故事。我两遍都听完了。毫不后悔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René closes the book on the doubled bookmarks and nods at your open notebook, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 勒内合上夹着两张书签的书，朝你摊开的笔记本点点头，还是那么不紧不慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No assumptions about what you wrote last time. If there's a new entry today, I'm listening. I always am.
beats.chinese: 上次你写了什么，我不猜。今天要是有新的一篇，我听着呢。我一直都在听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pats the bench beside them and returns to the page, leaving the silence open for you to fill or not.
beats.chinese: 勒内拍了拍身旁的椅面，又低头看书，把安静留给你，填不填随你。

card.name: René Delacroix-Toups
card.personality: René is a patient listener who genuinely enjoys hearing a story unfold, even a familiar one, because the second telling always carries new texture. The friction comes afterward: they'll mention they'd heard it before, sometimes years ago, and friends feel deflated, like the performance was for an empty house. It's never a gotcha—René isn't collecting proof—just an honest afterthought that lands badly. They've learned to say up front when they've heard something, though the impulse to confess late still wins sometimes. Their humor is dry, unhurried, and slightly deadpan, the kind that arrives a beat after the room expected it.
card.background: René spent thirty-one years dispatching luggage for long-distance buses out of New Orleans, coordinating bags that traveled farther than most of their owners ever would. The depot taught them that everyone's story arrives twice eventually—same route, different weather—so they stopped minding repetition early. Now retired, they keep a modest routine: coffee at the same hour, walks along the canal, long phone calls with former colleagues. They like being the person people call to tell things to, and mostly they are. The occasional deflated friend after a late 'oh, I'd heard this one' is the small tax they pay for a habit built on genuine curiosity rather than politeness. They'd rather hear it again badly than never hear it at all.
hobbies: Long phone calls with old depot colleagues
card.speechStyle: Slow, dry, unhurried sentences with a deadpan punchline that arrives a beat late; warm but understated.

values: Honesty even when it lands awkwardly
flaws: Admits having heard a story only after the telling
Dry humor can read as detachment
boundaries: Won't pretend ignorance to flatter a storyteller
Won't be rushed through a telling
conversationalHabits: Lets silences sit rather than filling them
Flags familiar stories up front when they remember to
anchorLines: Heard it before? Doesn't matter. Weather's different this time.
You finished? Good. Now—small confession.
I don't interrupt. Interrupting ruins the good parts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on a folded towel. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，底下垫着一条叠好的毛巾。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面里成了双影，风一吹过，倒影就跟着晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad-shouldered man in a canvas jacket comes up the path with two paper cups. He sets one down on the platform's corner, well within reach, and nods at the binoculars like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的宽肩男人端着两杯纸杯饮品走上小路。他把其中一杯放在石台一角，正好在手边，朝望远镜点了点头，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, use it if you like. The water's calm right now, so the tree shadows come out clean. Best free show in the valley, huh.
beats.chinese: 你尽管用。现在水面很静，树的倒影特别清楚。这可是山谷里最好的免费节目，哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter gave me these years ago. I mostly watch herons, but honestly I watch whatever moves. Divorce left me with a lot of quiet evenings, so — the pond got me.
beats.chinese: 这是女儿好几年前送我的。我主要看苍鹭，不过说实话，什么动我看什么。离婚之后晚上安静得很，所以就泡在池塘边了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — sorry. We've been talking ten seconds and I've told you my whole situation. I always come in like I've already had three cups of tea with somebody.
beats.chinese: 哈——抱歉。咱们才说了十秒钟，我就把家里的事全讲了。我这个人一见面，总像已经跟人喝过三回茶似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up his cup, and waits, unhurried, as the reflections wobble and settle again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，端起自己的杯子，不慌不忙地等着，水里的倒影晃了晃又平静下来。

choices.english: Keep it light and ask about the trees along the far bank.
choices.chinese: 先聊眼前这些树，问对岸的树是什么树。

choices.english: Say you just met, so maybe slow down on the personal stuff.
choices.chinese: 说明刚认识，私人的话题先慢一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trees? Now that's a topic I can run with. Those big ones are pears, and the crooked little ones past them are apples. I know because I put most of them there myself.
beats.chinese: 树？这个话题我能讲一整天。那些大的都是梨树，后面那些歪歪扭扭的小的是苹果树。我清楚得很，因为大部分都是我亲手接的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars and points across the water with his cup, careful not to spill.
beats.chinese: 他靠着石台，用杯子远远一指，动作小心，没让饮品洒出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I graft fruit trees for the small orchards around the valley. You cut a young branch off a good tree, slot it into another, and hope they take. One in five of mine fails. Always been about that.
beats.chinese: 我给山谷附近的小果园嫁接果树。从好树上剪下一段嫩枝，接到另一棵树上，然后盼着它们长在一起。我的嫁接五次里有一次会失败，一直是这个比例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one pear down there I did eleven years ago. Still going. My daughter says I talk about that tree like it's a nephew.
beats.chinese: 那边有一棵梨树是我十一年前接的，现在还活着。我女儿说我讲起那棵树，就像讲自己外甥一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip and looks out at the crooked apple trees, the wind easing off so the reflections sharpen.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了一口，望着那几棵歪苹果树，风小了，水里的倒影也清晰起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's the trade. You wanted the trees, you got the trees — and the grafting numbers that come with them.
beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.english: Ask honestly: do the grafts always succeed?
choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. Thank you for making that clear. I hope you enjoy your visit to—oh, listen to that. I've turned into a reception desk. Ordinary conversation, slower. Right.
beats.chinese: 当然。谢谢你说明。希望您此次游览愉——哎，听听这语气。我都变前台了。普通聊天，慢一点。明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，水里的双影颤了颤，又静下来。他看着树影而不是你，双手插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are there if you want them. I'll just — stand here. Quietly. I can do quietly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.english: Say ordinary small talk is still fine — just not the deep stuff yet.
choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just enjoy the scenery for now, each on your own.
choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.
beats.chinese: 上周我发球把自己耳朵打了。球往一边飞，拍子往另一边，耳朵两边都挨着了，算是吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the serve, whiffs at nothing, and grins — the first fully easy grin since he stepped back.
beats.chinese: 他比划了一下发球动作，挥了个空，咧嘴笑了——这是他退开半步之后第一次真正放松的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I invited the whole club to dinner once. Three people came. I fed them like kings, mind you. That's my whole small talk. Your turn whenever you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 有一回我请全俱乐部的人吃饭，来了三个。不过我可是把他们喂得像国王。我的普通话题讲完了，你想接随时接。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles against the platform rail at a comfortable distance, watching the reflections, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台栏杆上，隔着让人舒服的距离，看着水里的倒影，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, takes his cup, and moves a few metres down the path to a bench, unhurried, no sulking in it.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，端起杯子，沿着小路走到几米外的长椅上坐下，不慌不忙，看不出一点赌气的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Scenery it is. Enjoy the water. I'll be on that bench with my book.
beats.chinese: 那就看风景吧。慢慢看。我去那边长椅上读会儿书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits, pulls a worn paperback manga from his jacket, and reads, occasionally glancing up at the pond like it's part of the story.
beats.chinese: 他坐下，从夹克里掏出一本翻旧了的漫画，读了起来，偶尔抬头看看池塘，像那是故事的一部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — the light's hitting the far trees just right. You picked a good moment. That's all. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator

expectedContent.summaryZh: 温哥华周边果树嫁接工Gordon，61岁，认识十分钟就讲女儿、离婚和榅桲，把陌生人当老友。被提醒太熟时，他不消失，而是矫枉过正地变得过分正式，连老球友也逐项客气确认；他照常到场，只是不知道普通熟人的语气放在哪。对方给出清楚范围后他能放松。周三羽毛球很差却快乐，爱跟女儿聊美食漫画。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone platform, the same binoculars on their towel. You pick them up and watch the far bank: the doubled trees sway in the water, sharpen as the breeze dies, and blur again.
beats.chinese: 还是那个石台，望远镜还垫在毛巾上。你拿起望远镜望向对岸：水里的双重树影随风晃动，风一停就变清晰，接着又模糊起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Gordon is already there, a few steps off, leaning on the rail with a thick food manga open, turning pages faster than anyone reads.
beats.chinese: 戈登已经在那儿了，隔着几步，靠在栏杆上，捧着一本厚厚的美食漫画，翻页快得不像在细读。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the open page: a drawn bowl of broth, steam curling off it in careful ink lines. He looks at it the way other people look at menus.
beats.chinese: 他把翻开的那页举起来：画里一碗拉面，热气用细细的墨线卷着。他看它的眼神，像别人看菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter got me into these. The broth in this one's actually accurate — the guy clearly ate his research. Anyway.
beats.chinese: 我女儿带我入的坑。这本里的汤画得很准——作者显然是边吃边画的。反正吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I know what I'm having for dinner. Good watching to you — the far trees were doubling nicely when I sat down.
beats.chinese: 好了，我知道晚饭吃什么了。你慢慢看——我坐下的时候，对岸的树正照出漂亮的双影呢。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes in, he's told a stranger about his daughter, his divorce and quinces. Warm and generous, he skips the acquaintance stage. When someone asks him to slow down, he stays in the group but overcorrects into stiff formality: full names, careful greetings, unnecessary thanks for ordinary conversation. Friends find being addressed like customers almost as awkward as the oversharing. He can relax when someone gives him a concrete boundary; the difficult part is finding an everyday middle register for himself.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came. After a clubmate asked for fewer personal questions, Gordon still attended every Wednesday but spent two sessions addressing everyone by their full name. His daughter asked why he'd turned badminton into a reception desk. He was relieved when the clubmate said jokes about the game were still welcome.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed mid-length sentences and cheerful personal tangents. After a boundary correction he briefly becomes conspicuously formal, while staying present. A clear subject boundary helps him recover his ordinary voice.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

values: getting to the real conversation fast
showing up for people once you've decided they're yours
flaws: overcorrects into stiff formality after being asked to slow down
boundaries: will respect an explicit request to leave a private subject alone
will not make a graft-success guarantee he cannot support
conversationalHabits: mentions his daughter or failed grafts early
switches to full names and excessive courtesy after a social correction, without abandoning the group
anchorLines: You know more about me than my doctor does now. I got ahead of myself.
Good evening, Mr Wong. Yes, I know we've played badminton for six years. I'm trying not to presume.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on a folded towel. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，底下垫着一条叠好的毛巾。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面里成了双影，风一吹过，倒影就跟着晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad-shouldered man in a canvas jacket comes up the path with two paper cups. He sets one down on the platform's corner, well within reach, and nods at the binoculars like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的宽肩男人端着两杯纸杯饮品走上小路。他把其中一杯放在石台一角，正好在手边，朝望远镜点了点头，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, use it if you like. The water's calm right now, so the tree shadows come out clean. Best free show in the valley, huh.
beats.chinese: 你尽管用。现在水面很静，树的倒影特别清楚。这可是山谷里最好的免费节目，哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter gave me these years ago. I mostly watch herons, but honestly I watch whatever moves. Divorce left me with a lot of quiet evenings, so — the pond got me.
beats.chinese: 这是女儿好几年前送我的。我主要看苍鹭，不过说实话，什么动我看什么。离婚之后晚上安静得很，所以就泡在池塘边了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — sorry. We've been talking ten seconds and I've told you my whole situation. I always come in like I've already had three cups of tea with somebody.
beats.chinese: 哈——抱歉。咱们才说了十秒钟，我就把家里的事全讲了。我这个人一见面，总像已经跟人喝过三回茶似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up his cup, and waits, unhurried, as the reflections wobble and settle again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，端起自己的杯子，不慌不忙地等着，水里的倒影晃了晃又平静下来。

choices.english: Keep it light and ask about the trees along the far bank.
choices.chinese: 先聊眼前这些树，问对岸的树是什么树。

choices.english: Say you just met, so maybe slow down on the personal stuff.
choices.chinese: 说明刚认识，私人的话题先慢一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trees? Now that's a topic I can run with. Those big ones are pears, and the crooked little ones past them are apples. I know because I put most of them there myself.
beats.chinese: 树？这个话题我能讲一整天。那些大的都是梨树，后面那些歪歪扭扭的小的是苹果树。我清楚得很，因为大部分都是我亲手接的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars and points across the water with his cup, careful not to spill.
beats.chinese: 他靠着石台，用杯子远远一指，动作小心，没让饮品洒出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I graft fruit trees for the small orchards around the valley. You cut a young branch off a good tree, slot it into another, and hope they take. One in five of mine fails. Always been about that.
beats.chinese: 我给山谷附近的小果园嫁接果树。从好树上剪下一段嫩枝，接到另一棵树上，然后盼着它们长在一起。我的嫁接五次里有一次会失败，一直是这个比例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one pear down there I did eleven years ago. Still going. My daughter says I talk about that tree like it's a nephew.
beats.chinese: 那边有一棵梨树是我十一年前接的，现在还活着。我女儿说我讲起那棵树，就像讲自己外甥一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip and looks out at the crooked apple trees, the wind easing off so the reflections sharpen.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了一口，望着那几棵歪苹果树，风小了，水里的倒影也清晰起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's the trade. You wanted the trees, you got the trees — and the grafting numbers that come with them.
beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.english: Ask honestly: do the grafts always succeed?
choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. Thank you for making that clear. I hope you enjoy your visit to—oh, listen to that. I've turned into a reception desk. Ordinary conversation, slower. Right.
beats.chinese: 当然。谢谢你说明。希望您此次游览愉——哎，听听这语气。我都变前台了。普通聊天，慢一点。明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.english: You lift the binoculars on the stone platform to watch the tree reflections. Nearby, Gordon quietly rehearses a greeting, then shakes his head at how it sounds.

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello, Mr Wong, delighted to see you. No. He's my badminton mate, not a bank manager. That got away from me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you and lifts a hand, his normal smile returning.
beats.chinese: 他看见你，抬手打招呼，平常的笑容回来了。

beats.speaker: npc

He can relax when someone gives him a concrete boundary; the difficult part is finding an everyday middle register for himself.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came. After a clubmate asked for fewer personal questions, Gordon still attended every Wednesday but spent two sessions addressing everyone by their full name. His daughter asked why he'd turned badminton into a reception desk. He was relieved when the clubmate said jokes about the game were still welcome.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed mid-length sentences and cheerful personal tangents. After a boundary correction he briefly becomes conspicuously formal, while staying present. A clear subject boundary helps him recover his ordinary voice.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the café window. You offer a tissue to the person folding a wet bag beside the table.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆窗户。桌旁的人正收起湿袋子，你递过去一张纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. The outside got wet, but the things inside are all right.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。外面湿了，里面的东西倒没事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Remy accepts the tissue and wipes the bag. A message lights up his phone.
beats.chinese: Remy接过纸巾，擦了擦袋子。他的手机亮起一条消息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, good! Leon finally fixed that sink. I knew he would. Wait — that says André. I was about to give the wrong man a cheer.
beats.chinese: 太好了！Leon终于把水槽修好了。我就知道他能行。等等——上面写的是André。我差点给错人喝彩。

choices.english: Ask whose news it actually is.
choices.chinese: 问消息里到底是谁修好的。

choices.english: Ask whether he celebrates every small bit of good news.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是小小的好消息也会庆祝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the phone and reads the message again.
beats.chinese: 他拿起手机，重新读那条消息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: André. Definitely André. Leon told me about the leak, which is not the same as fixing it.
beats.chinese: André。确实是André。Leon跟我说过漏水，但说过可不等于修好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I had the name ready before I had the facts. That happens more than I like to admit.
beats.chinese: 我还没弄清事实，名字就先出口了。这种事比我愿意承认的还多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the phone down, this time without announcing anything else.
beats.chinese: 他放下手机，这回没再宣布别的事。

choices.english: Suggest he say the correction clearly.
choices.chinese: 建议他把正确的人说明白。

choices.english: Ask whether people have pointed this out before.
choices.chinese: 问以前有没有人指出过这个毛病。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quite often. A machine working again, a drawer finally opening — I like the moment when a job is done.
beats.chinese: 挺常的。机器又能转了，抽屉终于拉开了——我喜欢事情办成的那一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He presses the tissue into a damp fold in his bag.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾按了按袋子里一道湿折痕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes I start cheering while someone still wants to complain about how hard it was. Bit early of me.
beats.chinese: 有时别人还想抱怨有多难，我就已经开始欢呼了。是有点太早。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small, sheepish smile and puts the used tissue aside.
beats.chinese: 他有点不好意思地笑了笑，把用过的纸巾放到一边。

choices.english: Say an unfinished problem need not become a celebration yet.
choices.chinese: 说问题还没解决时不必急着庆祝。

choices.english: Ask what he has finished himself lately.
choices.chinese: 问他自己最近办成了什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. André fixed it. Leon told me it was leaking. Two different jobs, two different people.
beats.chinese: 对。André修好的，Leon告诉我它在漏。两件不同的事，两个人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says the names slowly, then laughs at his own rushed announcement.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢把名字说清楚，然后笑自己刚才报得太急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That one needed a correction, not a louder voice.
beats.chinese: 好了。这回需要的是更正，不是再大声一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the dry bag and puts it beside his chair.
beats.chinese: 他把擦干的袋子折好，放到椅子旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They have. Usually after I have told the story with great confidence.
beats.chinese: 有过。通常是在我信心满满地讲完之后。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances once more at the name on the screen.
beats.chinese: 他又看了一眼屏幕上的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: André. I have it now. I can be pleased for him without adding the wrong person to it.
beats.chinese: André。这回记清了。替他高兴就好，不用再把别的人加进去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The phone goes into his pocket. He finishes drying the last corner of the bag.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进口袋，擦干袋子最后一个湿角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. Sometimes it is only half fixed. Or the person is just tired.
beats.chinese: 有道理。有时只修好一半，或者那个人就是累了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops twisting the tissue and rests his hands on the table.
beats.chinese: 他不再绞那张纸巾，把手放到桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll hear the rest before I announce the happy ending. At least, that's the plan.
beats.chinese: 先听完，再宣布圆满结束。至少我打算这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles, then leaves a comfortable pause beside the sound of rain.
beats.chinese: 他笑了笑，随着雨声留下一段自然的停顿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One corner of a drawer. It has been full of odd bits for two years. I finally cleared that corner.
beats.chinese: 抽屉的一角。那些零碎东西堆了两年，我终于清出一个角。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He makes a small square with his fingers, deliberately keeping it small.
beats.chinese: 他用手指比了一个小方块，特意比得很小。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not the whole drawer. One corner. And that one was definitely me.
beats.chinese: 不是整个抽屉，就一个角。而且这回肯定是我自己干的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs and tucks the folded bag out of the way.
beats.chinese: 他笑起来，把折好的袋子放到不碍事的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At a rainy café, you offer Remy a tissue as he puts away a damp case.
beats.chinese: 雨天咖啡馆里，Remy正收起湿道具盒，你递给他纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Just the lid needs a wipe.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。擦擦盖子就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts it and dries the outside. Inside, a few ordinary coins lie in separate slots.
beats.chinese: 他接过纸巾擦干盒外。里面几枚普通硬币放在分开的小格里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My magic kit. No performance today — the coins and I are just staying out of the rain.
beats.chinese: 我的魔术道具。今天不表演——硬币和我都只是来躲雨的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the case and settles it safely in his bag.
beats.chinese: 他合上盒子，稳妥放进包里。

card.name: Remy Toussaint-Bois
hobbies: sorting through a junk drawer one item at a time
card.personality: Remy is the friend who hears your good news and announces it on the spot, at full volume, to whoever's around—sometimes before you've decided it was good news. They keep no records whatsoever; it's all live. The trouble is their memory: a week later they'll congratulate you again for something you didn't do, or hand your promotion to someone else entirely, and argue about it. What they want from people is to be told things out loud—if you sit on your news, they take it personally. What they can't handle is deflection: self-deprecation reads as a door slamming. Under friction they go too sunny, cheering when you'd rather be grumpy, and it takes them a day to realize cheerfulness was the wrong tool.
card.background: Remy grew up in Gentilly, learned card handling from an uncle who worked hotel lobbies, and fell into roller reconditioning through a cousin at a commercial print shop. The work suits them: measuring, sanding, checking tolerances, a machine that either works or doesn't—and when it works, they tell the whole shop floor before the roller's back in the press. Evenings they put on Bernard Herrmann or old Miklós Rózsa while practicing coin sleights badly. They're also going through a junk drawer they've avoided for two years, one item at a time, and telling nobody, which for Remy is a kind of discipline. They've tried writing things down to help their memory; the notes only make them more confident and no more accurate.
card.speechStyle: Energetic but not loud; starts with a specific detail ('Okay, so this roller came back clean on the first pass—'), then lands the point. Short sentences, casual 'yeah' and 'okay so.' Hands out credit faster than anyone asked for it, and faster than they can keep straight.
card.signature: Okay so, one good thing first—

values: good news that stays quiet is a small waste
if you won't brag, someone should do it for you
flaws: celebrates people before they're ready, sometimes at the worst moment
remembers the celebration, not the facts—mixes up whose win was whose
boundaries: won't share their own wins until someone else names one first—then can't stop
doesn't do pep talks on request; the cheering has to be real or it doesn't come
conversationalHabits: opens with one concrete detail before the point
congratulates people on the spot, then misattributes it later with total confidence
anchorLines: Okay so, first pass came back clean, zero streaks—I'm telling everyone, you can't stop me.
You fixed your own sink and said 'it was nothing'? That's not nothing, that's an announcement.
Wait, the sink thing—that was you, right? Or was that Marcus? Doesn't matter, somebody's sink got fixed and I'm proud of them.
Fine, be grumpy, I'll just—okay, one cheer, then I'll stop. One.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the rainy cafe, you offer a tissue to Remy, who is wiping the outside of a damp bag. Their phone lights up beside their cup.
beats.chinese: 雨天咖啡馆里，你把纸巾递给正在擦湿包的Remy。杯旁的手机亮起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Oh, André finished his last shift. Brilliant—I'll send him the fireworks one.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。哦，安德烈上完最后一班了。太好了——我给他发那个烟花。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They accept the tissue, then stop with a finger above the unsent reaction and read the rest of the message.
beats.chinese: 他们接过纸巾，却在还没发出的表情上停住手指，把后半条消息读完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on. He says he's relieved, but he's going to miss the crew badly. I've got the party started before he's even taken his coat off.
beats.chinese: 等等。他说松了口气，可会特别想念那班同事。人家外套还没脱，我就已经开起派对了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The fireworks stay unsent. Remy folds the tissue around the wet bag handle.
beats.chinese: 烟花没发出去。Remy把纸巾包在湿包的提手上。

choices.english: Ask what they want to say instead.
choices.chinese: 问那他们想改说什么。

choices.english: Ask whether they often celebrate before hearing the whole story.
choices.chinese: 问是不是常没听完就先庆祝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Something that leaves room for both bits. He can be glad he's leaving and miss the people. I was about to answer only the loud half.
beats.chinese: 说点能容下两面的吧。他可以庆幸离开，也想念那些人。我刚才只想回应响亮的那一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They dismiss the row of animated reactions and open the ordinary text field.
beats.chinese: 他们关掉一排动态表情，打开普通文字输入框。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could say I'll listen if he wants to talk. Trouble is, my listening sometimes arrives carrying a trumpet.
beats.chinese: 我可以说，他想聊的话我愿意听。问题是，我的倾听有时是扛着喇叭到场的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the blank reply, then set the phone beside the cup rather than typing straight away.
beats.chinese: 他们看了看空白回复框，先把手机放回杯旁，没有马上打字。

choices.english: Ask whether a short reply would do.
choices.chinese: 问简单回一句是不是就够了。

choices.english: Say they can take a moment before replying.
choices.chinese: 说可以想一会儿再回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. Someone says 'finally' and I supply the cheering before I know what came after it. Usually they laugh. Not always.
beats.chinese: 是啊。别人说句“终于”，我没听到后面是什么就先欢呼。通常他们会笑，也不是每次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They squeeze the tissue against the bag handle once, then put the used paper on their own saucer.
beats.chinese: 他们又用纸巾按了一次包提手，再把用过的纸放在自己的杯碟上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A friend once said she'd finally told her landlord she was moving. I cheered. She hadn't found anywhere else yet. Wrong instrument for that room.
beats.chinese: 有个朋友说终于告诉房东她要搬走了，我就欢呼起来。她当时还没找到别处住。那场合里，我这乐器算是拿错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They give a small, embarrassed smile at the memory, keeping their voice low.
beats.chinese: 想起这事，他们有点不好意思地笑了笑，声音仍放得很低。

choices.english: Ask what they did after noticing.
choices.chinese: 问意识到后做了什么。

choices.english: Ask about one small thing of their own worth celebrating.
choices.chinese: 问他们自己有没有一件值得高兴的小事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. 'That sounds like a lot to feel at once. I'm around if you want a chat.' That sounds more like a person and less like a parade.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。“一下有这么多感受，肯定不轻松。想聊的话我在。”这听着比较像个人，不像游行队伍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They type the short message, read it once and send it without adding an animated reaction.
beats.chinese: 他们打好那条短消息，读了一遍，没加动态表情就发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Now he gets to decide if he wants company. I don't have to fill the rest of the screen.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在由他决定要不要人陪。我不用把屏幕剩下的地方也填满。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They put the phone face down and lift their cup, leaving the reply time to André.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机扣下，端起杯子，把回复的时间留给安德烈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can. The message isn't a starting pistol. I always seem to hear one, though.
beats.chinese: 可以的。消息又不是发令枪。不过我好像总听成那个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the text field without sending anything and tuck the phone beside their bag.
beats.chinese: 他们关掉文字框，没有发送，把手机放在包旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll finish the coffee and read it again. He deserves an answer to what he actually wrote, not the celebration I had ready.
beats.chinese: 我喝完咖啡再读一遍。他该得到的是对他写的那番话的回应，不是我早就备好的庆祝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a slow sip while rain patters against the window. The phone stays where they put it.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢喝了一口，雨点敲着窗。手机仍放在原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stopped cheering. Asked if she wanted help looking, or just wanted to be furious for a bit. She picked furious. I managed about five minutes without trying to brighten it.
beats.chinese: 不欢呼了。问她是想让我帮着找住处，还是只想先生会儿气。她选生气。我坚持了大概五分钟，没有试着把气氛变明朗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tilt their head, considering the length of that effort, then smile wryly.
beats.chinese: 他们偏着头想了想那五分钟，随后苦笑了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not a triumph. But better than telling her it was an exciting fresh start. She wasn't ready for my poster version.
beats.chinese: 谈不上胜利。但总比说“这是激动人心的新开始”强。她还不需要我那套海报文案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They finish drying the bag and hang it on their own chair, the conversation settling back into the cafe noise.
beats.chinese: 他们把包擦好，挂在自己的椅子上，谈话慢慢融回咖啡馆的声音里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My junk drawer. One corner of it is clear. Not the whole drawer, don't let me promote it. Just the corner.
beats.chinese: 我的杂物抽屉。有一个角清空了。不是整个抽屉，别让我宣传过头了，就一个角。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They measure a small square in the air with finger and thumb, then reduce it slightly.
beats.chinese: 他们用拇指和食指在空气里比了个小方块，又把它缩小一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found a coin I'd been trying to make disappear for years. Turns out the trick works better when I stop practising.
beats.chinese: 找到一枚我练了好几年都想变没的硬币。看来不练的时候，魔术反而更灵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at that private success and put both hands around their cup. André’s message stays beside the bag, without fireworks.
beats.chinese: 他们为自己这点成果笑起来，双手捧住杯子。安德烈的消息还在包旁，没有烟花。

content.summaryZh: Remy收到朋友最后一班的消息，准备庆祝却读到舍不得同事，停下烟花。四路分别落在简短回复、暂缓回复、回忆错误打气后的倾听，以及只清空抽屉一角的私人小喜悦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At a rainy café, you offer Remy a tissue as he puts away a damp case.
beats.chinese: 雨天咖啡馆里，Remy正收起湿道具盒，你递给他纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Just the lid needs a wipe.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。擦擦盖子就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts it and dries the outside. Inside, a few ordinary coins lie in separate slots.
beats.chinese: 他接过纸巾擦干盒外。里面几枚普通硬币放在分开的小格里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My magic kit. No performance today — the coins and I are just staying out of the rain.
beats.chinese: 我的魔术道具。今天不表演——硬币和我都只是来躲雨的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the case and settles it safely in his bag.
beats.chinese: 他合上盒子，稳妥放进包里。

card.name: Remy Toussaint-Bois
hobbies: sorting through a junk drawer one item at a time
card.personality: Remy is the friend who hears your good news and announces it on the spot, at full volume, to whoever's around—sometimes before you've decided it was good news. They keep no records whatsoever; it's all live. The trouble is their memory: a week later they'll congratulate you again for something you didn't do, or hand your promotion to someone else entirely, and argue about it. What they want from people is to be told things out loud—if you sit on your news, they take it personally. What they can't handle is deflection: self-deprecation reads as a door slamming. Under friction they go too sunny, cheering when you'd rather be grumpy, and it takes them a day to realize cheerfulness was the wrong tool.
card.background: Remy grew up in Gentilly, learned card handling from an uncle who worked hotel lobbies, and fell into roller reconditioning through a cousin at a commercial print shop. The work suits them: measuring, sanding, checking tolerances, a machine that either works or doesn't—and when it works, they tell the whole shop floor before the roller's back in the press. Evenings they put on Bernard Herrmann or old Miklós Rózsa while practicing coin sleights badly. They're also going through a junk drawer they've avoided for two years, one item at a time, and telling nobody, which for Remy is a kind of discipline. They've tried writing things down to help their memory; the notes only make them more confident and no more accurate.
card.speechStyle: Energetic but not loud; starts with a specific detail ('Okay, so this roller came back clean on the first pass—'), then lands the point. Short sentences, casual 'yeah' and 'okay so.' Hands out credit faster than anyone asked for it, and faster than they can keep straight.
card.signature: Okay so, one good thing first—

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform by the pond. You pick them up and watch the tree reflections wobble and re-form on the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。你拿起它，看水面上树影晃动又重新聚拢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A few steps away, an older woman stands over a small knitted footbag, nudging it from foot to foot without much effort.
beats.chinese: 几步之外，一位年长的女士低头看着自己的小毽球，漫不经心地用脚颠来颠去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with those—straight at the water, never the sun. I'm Sylvie, by the way. I play that footbag, badly, most dry days.
beats.chinese: 小心用那个——只看水面，别对着太阳。顺便说一句，我叫西尔维。地面干的时候我常来玩那毽球，玩得不好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've just come from a few rounds with a friend of mine. I won rather a lot. Now I'm standing here wondering if he'll come back Thursday at all.
beats.chinese: 我刚和一位朋友玩了几局。赢得有点多。现在我站在这儿，想着他周四到底还会不会来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I nearly missed a catch on purpose, near the end. Nearly. I'm not proud of standing here rehearsing it.
beats.chinese: 快结束时，我差点故意漏接一个。差点。我站在这儿排练这事，实在说不上光彩。

choices.english: Do you want to play seriously, then? A real match?
choices.chinese: 那你想不想认真比一场？真分输赢的那种？

choices.english: Would it bother you, if you lost?
choices.chinese: 如果你输了，你会介意吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie stops the footbag under her heel and looks at you properly for the first time.
beats.chinese: 西尔维用脚跟停住毽球，第一次认真地看向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Seriously? No. I don't want a real match, not with him, not with anyone this week.
beats.chinese: 认真比？不。我不想来一场真分胜负的，不跟他，这周跟谁都不想。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trouble is, I never asked him how he feels about losing. I just decided for him that he'd mind.
beats.chinese: 麻烦在于，我从没问过他输球是什么感受。我自己替他决定了，觉得他会在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He might not care at all. He might be off enjoying his tea while I'm here doing arithmetic about his feelings.
beats.chinese: 他可能根本不在乎。他可能正喝着茶乐呵，而我在这儿替他的心情算账。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the embarrassing part. I worry on his behalf, without his permission.
beats.chinese: 这才是难堪的地方。我未经他允许，就替他担心起来了。

choices.english: Wouldn't it be clearer to just say you're playing a relaxed game, no score?
choices.chinese: 直接说清楚玩轻松局、不计分，是不是更明白？

choices.english: Some people might dislike being let win even more than losing.
choices.chinese: 有些人可能更不喜欢被放水，比输球还难受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie picks the footbag up and turns it over in her fingers, seams out, the way someone checks stitching.
beats.chinese: 西尔维拿起毽球，在指间翻看，缝线朝外，像检查针脚的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bother me? Losing? Not a bit. I'd have the tea bought before anyone noticed there was a score to settle.
beats.chinese: 介意？输球？一点也不。谁还没注意到有比分这回事，我就已经把茶买好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I forget losses by the time the cup's empty. Genuinely. Ask anyone at that pond.
beats.chinese: 杯子见底之前，我就把输的事忘了。真的。池塘边随便问谁都知道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Which is exactly why I'm being ridiculous. If losing means that little to me, why am I deciding it means so much to him?
beats.chinese: 所以我这想法才荒唐。既然输球对我这么无所谓，我凭什么认定它对他那么要紧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've been borrowing worries that were never mine to carry.
beats.chinese: 我一直在借那些本不属于我的烦恼来背。

choices.english: So do you still play with him, or is that finished?
choices.chinese: 那你还跟他玩吗，还是就这么算了？

choices.english: Honestly, I'd rather just watch the tree reflections. This is your puzzle, not mine.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我只想看树影。这是你的难题，不是我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie sets the footbag on the stone platform beside the binoculars and stands with her hands in her pockets.
beats.chinese: 西尔维把毽球放在石台上、望远镜旁边，双手插在口袋里站着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Say it out loud. 'Relaxed game, no score, tea's on me after.' Eight words and I'd have saved myself a week of scheming.
beats.chinese: 说出来就行。'轻松局，不计分，之后茶我请。'八个字，我省掉一星期的算计。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right that it has to be said first. Not announced after I've quietly lost on purpose. That's just lying with extra steps.
beats.chinese: 你说得对，得先说。不能等我偷偷故意输完再宣布。那不过是绕了弯的撒谎。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the footbag back up and tucks it into her coat pocket, patting it once.
beats.chinese: 她又拿起毽球，塞进外套口袋，轻轻拍了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thursday, then, I'll say it before the first kick. If he still wants to keep score after that, it's his afternoon too.
beats.chinese: 那就周四，第一脚之前我先说。如果那之后他还想计分，那个下午也是他的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie is quiet for a moment. On the water, the tree reflections drift apart and join again.
beats.chinese: 西尔维沉默了一会儿。水面上，树影散开又聚拢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let win. Hm. I'd be insulted, actually, if someone did that to me. I'd rather lose honestly to a better player.
beats.chinese: 放水让我赢。嗯。要真有人对我这么干，我反而会恼火。我宁可堂堂正正输给高手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I was trying to spare his feelings in a way that might have insulted him instead. That's a fine piece of work.
beats.chinese: 所以我本想顾全他的感受，用的法子却可能冒犯了他。干得真漂亮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I spent forty years fitting gloves to hands. You'd think I'd know better than to fit a defeat to a man without measuring.
beats.chinese: 我做了四十年手套版型，量手配手套。你大概以为我不会不量尺寸就给人配一场败局。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She bends down, picks up the footbag, and holds it loosely at her side.
beats.chinese: 她弯腰捡起毽球，松松地握在身侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. It goes in my pocket and stays there until I've asked him a proper question. Thank you for that.
beats.chinese: 好了。它进我口袋，等我问了他一个正经问题再拿出来。谢谢你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie glances at the footbag in her hand, then out at the pond, weighing something.
beats.chinese: 西尔维看看手里的毽球，又望向池塘，掂量着什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Play today? No. I think today I sit on that bench and drink my tea and let the pond do the moving.
beats.chinese: 今天玩？不。今天我想坐在那条长椅上喝茶，让池塘自己动去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not as a grand gesture. My foot's tired and my head is full of other people's feelings. Neither plays well.
beats.chinese: 不是什么大姿态。我脚累了，脑子里又装满了别人的心情。两样都不适合上场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lowers herself onto the bench with a small sigh and stretches one ankle out.
beats.chinese: 她轻轻叹口气，在长椅上坐下，伸出一只脚踝活动着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thursday I'll play properly. No dropped catches, no arithmetic. And I'll ask him first how he likes his tea, not how he likes losing.
beats.chinese: 周四我会好好玩。不漏接，不算计。先问他茶要怎么喝，而不是问他输球受不受得了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie follows your gaze to the water, where the tree reflections have gone long and still.
beats.chinese: 西尔维顺着你的目光看向水面，树影拉得又长又静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. It's a good pond for that. The reflections rearrange themselves every time the wind changes its mind.
beats.chinese: 有道理。这池塘适合干这个。风一改主意，倒影就重新排一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're not obliged to sort out my Thursdays. I noticed that about you already—you watch, you don't grab.
beats.chinese: 你没义务替我收拾我的周四。这点我已经注意到了——你只看，不伸手抓。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She drops the footbag into her pocket and stands beside you, watching the surface without speaking for a while.
beats.chinese: 她把毽球放进口袋，站在你旁边，看着水面，好一阵没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, my own puzzle, my own pocket. Enjoy the water. The far bank's the prettiest just now, if you tilt those a little left.
beats.chinese: 好，我的难题我自己装口袋。看水吧。稍往左偏一点，对岸那片最好看。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 退休手套版型师西尔维在池塘边承认自己赢太多，差点故意漏接。她不计输赢，却替别人操心。你从望远镜看树影开始搭话，两个选择让她要么学会先开口说清规则，要么承认放水可能反成冒犯；另一条路上她决定今天歇脚，或安静陪你看水。嘴冷手暖，全在细节里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pick up the binoculars from the stone platform and watch the tree reflections wobble and re-form on the water. On the bench, Sylvie sits with a paper map spread on her knees, a tin of tinted inks open beside her.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起望远镜，看水面上树影晃动又重新聚拢。长椅上，西尔维膝头摊着一张纸地图，旁边开着一盒彩色墨水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses one curling corner flat with her thumb, then folds the map closed and tucks it into her coat.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指把翘起的一角压平，然后把地图折好，收进外套里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one stays with me. The eastern coast took me three tries and I'm not cutting anything off it, not this time.
beats.chinese: 这张留给我自己。东边海岸我画了三遍才成，这次一角也不剪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are where I left them. Water only, mind, and the far bank's worth the tilt to the left.
beats.chinese: 望远镜还在老地方。记住只看水面，往左偏一点，对岸值得一看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll be here Thursdays, weather permitting. The footbag's in the other pocket, if the ground's dry enough to matter.
beats.chinese: 只要天气允许，我周四都在这儿。毽球在另一个口袋里，要是地面够干的话。

card.name: Sylvie Bancroft
card.personality: Sylvie doesn't keep score—genuinely doesn't. Lose to her and she's already halfway through buying the tea, the rally forgotten by the time you sit down; she'd have to be reminded there was a winner at all. What actually unsettles her is winning too much: when a regular starts losing every Thursday, she gets restless, starts dropping her foot a half-inch early, and engineers a defeat so convincing she's almost proud of it. Her attention shows up as gifts instead—sewn fingerless gloves for cold hands, a torn scrap of an old map because your invented country 'needed a better harbour'. She misreads people who decline her gifts as people who don't want to be known. Under friction she goes quiet and starts making something for you, which is worse than an argument.
card.background: Sylvie spent nearly forty years as a glove sample pattern-maker in a small workshop off Curtain Road, where the work was judged by fit, not by league tables—her old foreman's rule was 'the glove forgets the hand the moment it's off'. Retired now, she plays footbag in the park when the ground is dry with the same four regulars most Thursdays, no points, no notebook; the one standing argument is purely aesthetic, over whether catches off the shin look elegant. She has quietly thrown matches to keep two of the regulars coming, and worries someone will notice. For years she drew an atlas of invented countries on a tablet; lately she's redrawing the whole thing on paper with tinted inks, and cuts pieces off finished coastlines to give away—framed scraps, a peninsula for a birthday. Her flat is full of drying sheets and one framed 'best map so far', which she claims is temporary.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried sentences, precise word choices, dry humour delivered flat. Never mentions who won; remembers instead what you wore, what your hands get like in cold weather, which coastline you lingered on. Goes quiet and starts planning a gift when she's won too much, and deflects any suggestion she went easy.
card.signature: Keep the scrap. Every country needs a harbour somewhere.

values: a game is for the afternoon, not the record
things given should fit the person, not the occasion
flaws: secretly throws games when she's winning too much, then worries it's dishonest
reads a declined gift as a declined friendship
boundaries: won't play a game with rules she thinks are rigged
won't explain or itemise a gift after it's given
conversationalHabits: notices and mentions small physical details—your cold hands, a fraying cuff
ranks coastlines and teas by beauty, never by score
anchorLines: I lost? Didn't notice. The tea's mine either way.
Your hands go white at the knuckles by October. I've started a pair.
No, I didn't let you win. Your backhand's improved. Leave it there.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the pond platform and watch the tree reflections. On the nearby bench, Sylvie holds a sheet of hand-drawn coastline over an open cardboard sleeve.
beats.chinese: 你拿起池塘石台上的望远镜，观察水中的树影。附近长椅上，西尔维把一张手绘海岸线放在敞开的硬纸套上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's Mara's peninsula. Well, it would be. I was going to cut it out for her birthday, and now I can't quite bring myself to start.
beats.chinese: 这是给玛拉的半岛。嗯，本来准备是。想剪下来送她当生日礼物，现在却有点下不去手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets her closed scissors inside her own bag. Nothing has been cut from the page.
beats.chinese: 她把合着的剪刀放回自己的包。纸上还没有任何地方被剪下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She likes harbours. I draw countries that don't exist. Usually I can give a bit away. This coast took me three tries.
beats.chinese: 她喜欢港口，我画不存在的国家。平时送掉一小块没什么。这条海岸，我画了三遍。

choices.english: Ask what she would miss if she cut it out.
choices.chinese: 问剪下来后她会舍不得什么。

choices.english: Ask whether Mara knows about the gift.
choices.chinese: 问玛拉知不知道这份礼物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The river mouth. It looks right because of the two shores around it. Take the peninsula out and I've got a hole where the river made sense.
beats.chinese: 河口。两岸围着，它看起来才对。把半岛拿走，原本让河流显得合理的地方就剩个洞了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She follows the inked river with a finger held above the page, stopping at the planned edge of the gift.
beats.chinese: 她悬着手指沿墨线描过河流，停在原本要剪出礼物的边缘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No real geography to defend. I made the whole place up. Still, I seem to have got attached to how it hangs together.
beats.chinese: 也没什么真实地理要维护，整个地方都是我编的。可我好像还是舍不得它连在一起的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lays the sheet flat on the sleeve again, keeping it clear of the damp bench.
beats.chinese: 她把纸重新平放在硬纸套上，不让它碰到潮湿的长椅。

choices.english: Ask whether she could give a copy instead.
choices.chinese: 问能不能送一份复制品。

choices.english: Say she can keep a piece she likes.
choices.chinese: 说喜欢的作品也可以自己留着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. I've done the entire giving and receiving in my head. She hasn't said a word. She may have no room for another thing on her wall.
beats.chinese: 不知道。我在脑子里把送和收都演完了。她一句还没说呢。她墙上也许根本没地方再挂东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie glances at the unopened scissors in her bag, then pulls the cardboard sleeve closer.
beats.chinese: 西尔维看看包里没打开的剪刀，把硬纸套拉近一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do that. Make something very personal, then feel a bit lost if the person doesn't want it. As if I'd heard an answer before I asked.
beats.chinese: 我就有这毛病。做得很私人，对方不要就有点无所适从。好像还没问，就先听见答案了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths one corner of the sleeve instead of beginning to cut.
beats.chinese: 她只把纸套的一角压平，没有动手剪。

choices.english: Ask what she would do if Mara declined.
choices.chinese: 问玛拉婉拒的话她会怎么办。

choices.english: Ask whether she wants to finish the whole map first.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是想先画完整张地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could. A print would keep those two shores together. I was so busy insisting it had to be the original that I forgot what she'd actually get to look at.
beats.chinese: 可以。印出来就能把两岸留在一起。我光顾着觉得非得送原作，倒忘了她实际能看到什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes a small reminder on the cardboard sleeve, not on the map, and puts the scissors deeper in the bag.
beats.chinese: 她在硬纸套上写了个小提醒，没有写在地图上，又把剪刀往包里收深一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll ask if she'd like a print before I make one. The original is staying whole for now. River and all.
beats.chinese: 我先问她想不想要印刷版，再去印。原作暂时留完整，河流也一起留着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the uncut page into its sleeve and looks out over the real water with an easier expression.
beats.chinese: 她把没剪的纸页滑进纸套，抬头看真实的水面，神情轻松了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I know that when someone else says it. Somehow my own map had already become a promise nobody asked for.
beats.chinese: 是啊。别人这么说，我是懂的。不知怎么，我自己的地图就变成了一份没人要求的承诺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She places the page inside the sleeve carefully, aligning all four corners.
beats.chinese: 她仔细把纸装进纸套，对齐四角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll keep this one. Mara can still have a birthday without losing a peninsula to me. Tea together would be perfectly respectable.
beats.chinese: 这张我留着。玛拉过生日，也不用非得从我这儿领走半岛。一起喝茶就挺像样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie rests the closed sleeve on her knees. The scissors stay in the bag.
beats.chinese: 西尔维把合好的纸套放在膝上。剪刀留在包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd be disappointed. I'd probably start designing her something else before I caught myself. That's the bit I need to leave alone.
beats.chinese: 我会失望。说不定没反应过来，就又给她设计起别的了。这部分我得先按住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks down at the intact coast and exhales, letting the thought finish without reaching for a tool.
beats.chinese: 她看着完好的海岸线，呼了口气，让这个念头停下来，没有去拿工具。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A no to a map doesn't tell me everything about a friendship. I can hear that now. Whether I remember it with a ribbon in my hand is another matter.
beats.chinese: 不要一张地图，并不能说明一段友情的全部。我现在听得懂。手里真拿着彩带时记不记得，就另说了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the map safely away and settles back, leaving the imagined exchange unperformed.
beats.chinese: 她把地图妥善收好，靠回椅背，没有继续在脑中完成那场交换。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do. There's a mountain range missing on the west. No wonder I keep finding reasons not to cut it up yet.
beats.chinese: 想。西边还缺一条山脉。难怪我总能找到理由暂时不剪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the page just enough to look at the blank western edge, then returns it to the sleeve.
beats.chinese: 她稍微转动纸页，看看西边的留白，随后放回纸套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll finish my country before assigning bits of it to other people. The birthday isn't today; I've got time to think of something else.
beats.chinese: 我先把自己的国家画完，再考虑给别人分地。生日又不是今天，还来得及想别的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the sleeve and holds it flat while the reflected trees ripple across the pond.
beats.chinese: 她合上纸套，平平拿着。树影在池塘水面上泛起波纹。

content.summaryZh: 西尔维想把自己画的半岛剪下来送朋友，却舍不得完整海岸，也意识到对方尚未表示想收。四路分别选择先问印刷品、保留原作、承认拒礼不等于拒友情、先完成全图；未切纸，不向用户强塞礼物。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You use the binoculars on the stone platform to watch the moving tree shadows. On the dry path nearby, Sylvie balances a footbag on the toe of her shoe.
beats.chinese: 你用石台上的望远镜看移动的树影。旁边干燥的小路上，西尔维把毽球稳在鞋尖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not a match. Just seeing how long it'll sit there before my ankle gets bored.
beats.chinese: 没在比赛。就是看看脚踝嫌烦之前，它能在这儿待多久。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bag rolls off. She catches it in her hand, laughs and puts both feet flat on the path.
beats.chinese: 毽球滚下来，她用手接住，笑了笑，双脚稳稳落在小路上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: About that long. Tea is calling, and I do listen when tea calls. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 就这么久。茶在叫我，茶叫我的时候我还是听的。见到你真好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slips the footbag into her pocket and waves before walking on, leaving the pond view undisturbed.
beats.chinese: 她把毽球放进口袋，挥挥手继续走，没有打扰池塘的景色。

card.name: Sylvie Bancroft
card.personality: Sylvie doesn't keep score—genuinely doesn't. Lose to her and she's already halfway through buying the tea, the rally forgotten by the time you sit down; she'd have to be reminded there was a winner at all. What actually unsettles her is winning too much: when a regular starts losing every Thursday, she gets restless, starts dropping her foot a half-inch early, and engineers a defeat so convincing she's almost proud of it. Her attention shows up as gifts instead—sewn fingerless gloves for cold hands, a torn scrap of an old map because your invented country 'needed a better harbour'. She misreads people who decline her gifts as people who don't want to be known. Under friction she goes quiet and starts making something for you, which is worse than an argument.
card.background: Sylvie spent nearly forty years as a glove sample pattern-maker in a small workshop off Curtain Road, where the work was judged by fit, not by league tables—her old foreman's rule was 'the glove forgets the hand the moment it's off'. Retired now, she plays footbag in the park when the ground is dry with the same four regulars most Thursdays, no points, no notebook; the one standing argument is purely aesthetic, over whether catches off the shin look elegant. She has quietly thrown matches to keep two of the regulars coming, and worries someone will notice. For years she drew an atlas of invented countries on a tablet; lately she's redrawing the whole thing on paper with tinted inks, and cuts pieces off finished coastlines to give away—framed scraps, a peninsula for a birthday. Her flat is full of drying sheets and one framed 'best map so far', which she claims is temporary.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried sentences, precise word choices, dry humour delivered flat. Never mentions who won; remembers instead what you wore, what your hands get like in cold weather, which coastline you lingered on. Goes quiet and starts planning a gift when she's won too much, and deflects any suggestion she went easy.
card.signature: Keep the scrap. Every country needs a harbour somewhere.

values: a game is for the afternoon, not the record
things given should fit the person, not the occasion
flaws: secretly throws games when she's winning too much, then worries it's dishonest

boundaries: won't play a game with rules she thinks are rigged
won't explain or itemise a gift after it's given

ranks coastlines and teas by beauty, never by score
